title: P1 — bunker-mvp systemd-logind wedge is UNMONITORED: 46 bunkerd spawn failures in 24h (2026-10-14) produced zero alerts and zero board rows — only the mischief-chaos satellite's two SKIPped plane folds surfaced it
reasoning:
Found 2026-10-14 while triaging two consecutive mischief-chaos plane SKIPs (CHAOS-3, mischief board). Symptom on the fleet side: bunker-mvp answered `bunker list` with 4/50 agents, ssh up 12 days, / 61% used, 12G RAM available — yet every spawn died at stage rootless-install with "enable linger for bunker-<id>: Could not enable linger: Connection timed out".

LIVE EVIDENCE (measured this tick, ssh root@bunker-mvp):
- systemd-logind PID 24775 had been up 12 days, RSS 299MB, state R, holding 178 entries in /run/systemd/sessions.
- `busctl introspect org.freedesktop.login1 .../Manager` TIMED OUT (25s cap, empty output), while org.freedesktop.systemd1 and org.freedesktop.hostname1 on the SAME system bus both answered — so the wedge is logind-specific, not a dbus outage.
- `loginctl list-users` -> "Failed to list users: Connection timed out".
- bunkerd journal, 24h window: 46 "enable linger" failures; failing agent ids include 40306bbb, 59112a6a, eb84b8d4, 40d13b0d, 3860f968, b80b877b, 98823e1a, cc2e8a54, 5158ec82, ef382842. Per-hour failure line counts: Oct 14 02h=779, 03h=289, 04h=198, 05h=502.
- Remediation applied at 05:47Z: `systemctl restart systemd-logind` (Stopping 05:45:35, Started 05:47:05, new PID 2081843). After: 0 linger failures in the following 10+ minutes, logind RSS 299MB -> 26MB, and a plane run immediately PASSED (agent f27e5e74, TEARDOWN-GONE).

THE GAP: the monitoring stack has NO signal for this class. Nothing scrapes bunkerd's journal, nothing alerts on spawn-failure rate, nothing checks logind D-Bus liveness, and no exporter publishes agent counts or destroy-refused state. A host that is up, has disk, has RAM, and answers the bunker API can be completely unable to spawn agents for hours and the fleet sees nothing. It was discovered only because a chaos satellite's fold exit code went 3 twice.

ASK (stack work, belongs in /root/fleet-monitoring on fleet-monitor): (1) a bunkerd log-based alert — count of "enable linger"/"spawn agent failed"/"spawn failed" lines per host per 30m window > 0 for two consecutive windows = warning, > 5 = critical; (2) a logind liveness probe — `timeout 10 busctl introspect org.freedesktop.login1 /org/freedesktop/login1 org.freedesktop.login1.Manager` exit nonzero = critical (this catches the wedge ~hours before the spawn failures accumulate); (3) optionally an agent-state exporter publishing per-server agent count and destroy-refused count so the "4/50 but nothing spawns" contradiction is visible on a dashboard.

Cross-reference: mischief board CHAOS-3 (the two SKIPs this produced, now closed with the retry PASS) and MISCHIEF-DF-24 (bunker destroy refuses while any agent process is alive — same unreapable-agent family; three agents fa70ebf7/cb880c25/19d03bc5 still sit in destroy-refused:live_processes holding ~37.6G as of this tick).

title: MON-GAP-030 — the spool drain dedupes by row-id PRESENCE only, so an alert that re-fires after its row is closed is swallowed: DiskFull on bunker-mvp fired 4x on 2026-10-20 and landed nowhere
reasoning:
WHY: drain-board-rows.sh decides whether a spooled row is a duplicate by grepping the target board for the quoted row id and skipping on any hit. Row ids are MON-<LANE>-<FP8>-<YYYYMMDD> (alert fingerprint + UTC date), so the SECOND and later firings of the same condition on the same day reuse the first firing's id. The moment the first row is closed (status complete/done), every later firing of that same condition is silently swallowed and the live alert has no open work item — the alert-becomes-no-executed-work failure this lane exists to prevent. EVIDENCE (live, 2026-10-20): spool /tmp/fleet-monitoring-spool/board-rows.jsonl (732 lines, mtime 15:15Z) carries DiskFull-on-bunker-mvp firing rows at 13:03Z, 13:42Z, 14:07Z, 15:15Z each with a -RESOLVED twin; the board's row for that id was closed verification-only at 09:26Z; the 15:54Z drain reported appended=0 skipped=732 with zero unwritable rows; the alert was still firing at 15:58Z with bunker-mvp / at 100% (688M free). WITNESS: live:fleet-monitor:9090 + spool replay. The same shape hides repeats of every alert class whose first row of the day is closed — the drain cannot tell 'already handled and open' from 'handled, closed, and now firing again'.

FIX SHAPE (dispatched to a worker this tick): in drain-board-rows.sh, when a spooled FIRING row's id is present on the board, classify the board rows carrying that id — TERMINAL = complete/done/closed/verified-benign/duplicate/rejected/unverified-expired, anything else OPEN. title: Drain is not idempotent for alert-resolved rows: classifier reads tasks.jsonl while apply writes events.jsonl, so every run re-appends the same RESOLVED ids
reasoning:
Measured 2026-10-23 02:06Z on the monitoring lane box.

SYMPTOM: every drain run reports appended=4 for the same four alert-resolved ids, and /home/kara/monitoring/.coding-hermes/board/events.jsonl (382 lines) holds 193 duplicate copies of just four ids: MON-MONITORING-FA5F538B-20261022-RESOLVED x90, MON-MONITORING-B8283F46-20261022-RESOLVED x71, MON-MONITORING-FA5F538B-20261023-RESOLVED x20, MON-MONITORING-33D26594-20261023-RESOLVED x12. Two consecutive drain runs this tick each appended the same 4 (first run appended=4 skipped=842, second run appended=4 skipped=842).

ROOT CAUSE (source): ~/.hermes/scripts/drain-board-rows.sh classify stage builds bpath = <board_root>/<lane>/.coding-hermes/board/tasks.jsonl and looks for an existing row with that id; the apply stage routes type=alert-resolved rows to events.jsonl instead. An alert-resolved id therefore NEVER matches in tasks.jsonl -> 'id absent from the board' -> decision append, on every run. The script header claims 'Idempotent: a row whose id is already on the target board is skipped', so this is a contract violation, not intended behaviour. board_append.py is append-only by design and does no dedupe on its own.

REPRODUCTION (no write): DRY=1 MON_REMOTE=fleet-monitor bash ~/.hermes/scripts/drain-board-rows.sh -> 'DRY would append MON-MONITORING-B8283F46-20261022-RESOLVED ... events.jsonl' for all four ids that are ALREADY present 12-90 times. Evidence captured at /home/kara/.hermes/stand-in/monitoring/mischief/drain-20261023-0201.log and the DRY output in the same workdir.

IMPACT: unbounded growth of the audit event log (one line per drain run per historical resolved alert; the spool is cumulative so this never decays), noisy board diffs on every tick commit, and the drain's own 'appended=N' number is meaningless as a landed-row count. No alert loss observed - findings still land on tasks.jsonl correctly.

FIX DIRECTION: in the classify stage, select the presence-check path by row type (alert-resolved -> events.jsonl, else tasks.jsonl) exactly as the apply stage does, and dedupe events by id. Acceptance: with the current cumulative spool, two consecutive non-DRY drain runs report appended=0 on the second run; events.jsonl gains zero lines on a re-run; a genuinely NEW alert-resolved id still appends exactly once; the existing 193 duplicate lines are compacted only by an explicit opt-in repair, never silently.

DEDUPE CHECK: MON-GAP-030 (dedupe by id presence only, re-fire) and MON-DOGFOOD-047 (re-fire rows vs boardctl one-row-per-id canon) are different defects; MON-DOGFOOD-041 is the resolution-events-to-events.jsonl fix this exposed.
worker_summary: Fixed two defects: (a) resolved-event replay (dedupe now events.jsonl U tasks.jsonl), (b) unserialized concurrent drains (flock, rc=3 refusal). 13/13 new checks, 22/22 MON-GAP-030 regression, live drain appended=1 then 0.
resolution:
FIXED 2026-10-23 (tick monitoring-foreman-2026-10-23-02-39-23). ROOT CAUSE: the classifier in ~/.hermes/scripts/drain-board-rows.sh deduped EVERY row id against the lane's tasks.jsonl, while the apply loop routes type=alert-resolved rows to events.jsonl. A -RESOLVED spool line therefore never matched its own already-written event and was re-appended on every drain run. MEASURED DAMAGE: the live board carried 235 alert-resolved event lines for 13 unique ids (MON-MONITORING-FA5F538B-20261022-RESOLVED x98, B8283F46-20261022-RESOLVED x79, FA5F538B-20261023-RESOLVED x28, 33D26594-20261023-RESOLVED x20).
